title: Cohort Slicer: Guided Multi-Variant Split Composer and Emergency Quarantine Prototype
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Context: Platform teams want a low-friction way to split traffic across multiple model variants while keeping a tight safety envelope. Current Canvas-style rollout UIs at Redwood are powerful but assume linear staged ramps. This ticket explores a cohort-centric composer that treats audiences as independent slices (geo, customer-tier, header, percentage) and enables rapid quarantine and rollback of individual cohorts without impacting others.

Problem: Engineers and PMs need to perform targeted experiments (A/B and multi-variant) with the option to rapidly isolate problematic cohorts. Existing flows force either global rollback or complex manual edits. We need a visual composer that: 1) makes cohort definitions clear, 2) shows per-cohort health signals and relative cost impact, 3) supports quick quarantine/undo, and 4) provides predictable guardrails for automated ramps.

Design goals: 
- Make cohort creation fast: create, preview, and save in under 90s for a common use case.
- Surfaced observability: per-cohort latency, error-rate, token-cost-per-request, and sample outputs.
- Fail-safe actions: quarantine variant, swap to baseline, and time-limited holds with reason capture.
- Support multi-variant splits (up to 4 variants) and mixed routing (percent + attribute filters).
- Handoff-ready assets: component spec, interaction doc, and Figma prototype links.

Constraints & assumptions: 
- Backend will provide per-cohort metrics and an emergency toggle API (spiked with ENG-7428).
- Designer to assume a max of 4 cohorts visible at once; overflow uses accordion.
- Accessibility: color-independent status indicators required.

Deliverables: 
- Low-fidelity flow diagram and interaction map.
- Hi-fidelity Figma prototype with 3 key screens: composer, cohort detail flyout, and emergency quarantine modal.
- Component inventory (split slider, cohort chips, signal badges, quick-rollback CTA).
acceptance_criteria: Hi-fidelity Figma prototype completed and linked
Designer notes include component props and keyboard interactions
Usability test: 5 internal engineers complete 'create split and quarantine' task with success rate >= 80%
Design review sign-off from PM, Eng Lead, and Product Research
Hand-off package uploaded to Drive including annotated flows and exportable tokens
comments: 2026-02-11 | Sofia Reyes (PM): Liked the cohort-first approach. Request: show estimated token-cost delta per cohort in the composer canvas.
2026-02-18 | Ethan Kim (Eng): Backend spike returns per-cohort metrics; need a compact payload to keep UI updates under 200ms. We'll implement a partial streaming feed for top-level numbers.

2026-02-25 | Priya Sharma (Research): Ran 5 quick sessions with platform engineers. Confusion point: users expected the 'quarantine' action to reassign traffic to baseline automatically. Recommend the modal default to 'swap to baseline' with an option 'pause only'.
2026-03-03 | Marcus Nguyen (Design, assignee): Updated prototype to include cost delta chips and new 'swap to baseline' default. Shared updated link in design_links.
2026-03-09 | Liam O'Connor (Security): Please ensure audit log metadata includes actor, timestamp, and rollback reason. Also flagged that quarantine must honor RBAC roles.
decision_log: 2026-02-14 | Decided to surface three signal tiers: green/yellow/red with numeric badges, and include textual status for color-blind accessibility.
2026-02-19 | Opted for cohort-first composer instead of timeline-first to simplify multi-variant experiments.
2026-03-01 | Chose 'swap to baseline' as the emergency default behavior to minimize customer-visible regressions.
2026-03-05 | Bounded visible cohorts to 4; extra cohorts collapse into an accordion to reduce visual complexity.
usability_notes: Keyboard: composer supports arrow-key navigation between cohort chips; Enter to open details; Escape to cancel edits.
Screen reader: cohort chip announces name, variant, percent, and status.
Mobile: composer collapses to card list; emergency actions hidden behind a long-press to reduce accidental taps.
